findings.problem: Article36(b) requires both timely filing and payment of the tax declared. The personal Guide states only timely filing. The other two penalty summaries omit this scoped exception.
findings.fix: Say: If the return and the declared tax were both filed/paid on time and the later difference is no more than JOD5,000, the late charge on the difference runs from notification of the audit decision; above that, art.36(a) applies. Keep the currentness hold. Make the other summaries carry or explicitly cross-reference these conditions.

findings.problem: Imported-service timing loses both partial-payment/service triggers and their proportional limits.
findings.fix: State one month from paying the service fee or any part, to the extent relating to that part; customs release of the item carrying the service; or six months from receiving the service or any part, to the extent relating to that part, whichever applies first. Preserve Director-approved deferral and currentness hold.

findings.problem: Overview says foreign income is taxed only when funded from Jordan, omitting art.3(c)(2) foreign-branch income. Its social-security headline omits ordinary full-coverage scope, and1% monthly interest omits the art.19(a)(2)60-day-from-employment condition.
findings.fix: Include the foreign-branch route with audited final statements, or expressly limit the sentence to resident individuals. Put ordinary full-coverage employment beside14.25%/7.5%. Add the60-day source condition and distinguish source-baseline interest from a current assessment.

findings.problem: Interest/deposit withholding rows omit the taxable-income qualification and domestic bank/financial-company payer condition; corporate row also omits interbank and designated-recipient exceptions. These are explicit neighbors in art.12(a)(2).
findings.fix: Restrict the rows to taxable interest/commissions/qualifying deposit profits paid by banks and financial companies in Jordan; carry the interbank and executive-instruction exclusions beside the corporate figure or state that entitlement remains held until the full exclusion check is made. Preserve finality distinctions.

findings.problem: Some GST positive legal extracts exceed the actually readable evidence: special tax computed first has no supporting clause here; no input in the exempt row is not proved by a schedule-list title; purchases/imports and pre-registration deduction clauses are truncated. The Guide asserts deduction art.19 and refund art.20(d) although the author ledger explicitly says these article numbers were not established.
findings.fix: Read and quote complete official clauses and establish the article numbers, or move the unsupported portion/number to an explicit hold. Retain the readable sales-return and bad-debt material, and the50-500 nonresident departure refund amounts as conditional clause extracts with an article-number hold. Do not clear positive input entitlement using damaged OCR.

findings.problem: National-contribution cessation in art.11(g) applies to all art.11(f), but only the other-companies row states it. The half-year advance due-date row omits the express executive-instruction longer-period exception.
findings.fix: Use a common note beside all national-contribution rows/headline stating art.11(g) applies to every rate and its actual trigger is not cleared. Add unless executive instructions allow a longer period to the advance deadline.
